comparison: Perfect agreement on main conclusions (C3, C4, C65, C66). Both OpenEval and all three peer reviewers affirm the identification of degenerate cardiolipin binding motifs and the molecular determinants. OpenEval notes systematic analysis across ROCKET variants; peer reviewers explicitly state findings are 'convincing' with one noting 'the identification of degenerate cardiolipin binding motifs, the characterization of their dynamic features.'

Strong agreement on counterintuitive findings (C5, C6, C82, C83). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the surprising lack of correlation between binding affinity and stability. OpenEval describes 'complex patterns' and 'non-intuitive effects'; Reviewer 2 states 'Surprisingly, there appears to be no direct correlation' and Reviewer 3 explains this 'may be at first sight counterintuitive but actually matches expectations.'

Perfect agreement on cryo-EM validation (C49, C50, C51). Both evaluations support the structural confirmation findings. OpenEval notes appropriate resolution reporting and qualified interpretation of diffuse density; peer reviewers accept cryo-EM as part of 'state-of-the-art experimental approaches' without critique.

Perfect agreement on variant analysis (C60-C64). Both evaluations affirm the statistical significance and conclusions about core destabilization. OpenEval notes n=4 replicates with p-values; Reviewer 3 explicitly confirms mutations 'are experimentally verified by native mass spectrometry' and demonstrate key principles.

Strong agreement on CG-MD simulation findings (C36-C41). OpenEval provides detailed support for distinct binding modes, occupancies, and residence times over 50 µs; peer reviewers accept simulation findings as part of integrated approach, with Reviewer 1 noting 'coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation with the state-of-the-art experimental approaches' produces convincing findings.

Strong agreement on computational findings (C44-C48). OpenEval supports claims about redirected binding and increased force requirements from gas-phase MD; peer reviewers affirm these as part of integrated approach, with Reviewer 3 stating findings 'match expectations from structural data and MD modelling.'

Strong agreement on GlpG CDL binding characterization (C70-C75). OpenEval notes converging evidence from thermal shift, CG-MD, and native MS showing high occupancy and exclusive binding; Reviewer 1 explicitly states authors 'identify a stabilizing CDL site within the E. coli rhomboid intramembrane protease GlpG' and Reviewer 3 confirms thermal stabilization findings.

Strong agreement on native MS findings from proteoliposomes (C52-C55). OpenEval supports CDL preference and quantified intensity reduction; peer reviewers explicitly affirm native MS as key approach with Reviewer 2 noting 'State-of-the-art approaches and sharply focused experimental investigation lend credence to the conclusions drawn.'

Strong agreement on functional regulation findings (C76-C78, C85-C86). OpenEval notes protease activity assays with p<0.0001 significance establishing CDL as functional regulator; Reviewer 1 explicitly states study 'uncover[s] its regulatory influence on enzyme substrate preference' and both reviewers affirm this as key discovery.

Partial overlap on native MS findings (C56-C57). OpenEval supports differential monomer release and stabilization inference; peer reviewers accept native MS findings broadly as part of comprehensive validation, with Reviewer 3 confirming mutations are 'experimentally verified by native mass spectrometry.'

Strong agreement on integrated functional conclusions (C7-C8, C79-C80). OpenEval integrates multiple evidence lines establishing functional CDL regulation with structural mechanism; peer reviewers explicitly affirm regulatory findings with Reviewer 1 noting discovery of 'regulatory influence on enzyme substrate preference' as providing 'much needed insight.'

Partial overlap on database analysis and GlpG site identification (C67-C69). OpenEval supports bimodal distribution analysis and site identification; peer reviewers accept broader analysis extending to native proteins, with Reviewer 1 noting study addresses 'de novo-designed and native membrane proteins.'

Agreement with nuanced difference on Aac2 comparison (C87-C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting C88 functional consequences rely on cited work rather than presented data; peer reviewers accept Aac2 comparison as supporting evidence for generalizable principles without raising concerns about reliance on citations.

Agreement on methodological limitations (C90-C93). OpenEval supports these as appropriate acknowledgment of gas-phase and MS limitations; peer reviewers implicitly accept limitations as reasonable caveats, with editor noting 'authors addressed all reviewer comments adequately and rigorously.'

Partial overlap on study limitations and contributions (C94-C96). OpenEval supports discussion of ROCKET limitations and key conceptual contribution; peer reviewers accept these as reasonable caveats that don't undermine conclusions.

Strong agreement on overarching conclusion (C96). OpenEval supports main insight about complexity of lipid-protein interactions; all three peer reviewers explicitly affirm this conclusion, with Reviewer 1 stating findings 'will provide much needed insight' and Reviewer 2 noting work 'provides much-needed insight into the poorly understood nature of protein-CDL interactions.'

OpenEval evaluated background/context claims (C1-C2, C9-C35) as appropriately cited prior work establishing context. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel findings.

OpenEval evaluated C59 (ROCKET validation) as supported by experimental data and appropriate citations. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate this validation claim, treating ROCKET as an accepted model system throughout their reviews.
